open.speaker: hollis
lines: Bragg. Dam crew. I do your wagon's oil 'cause Dot pays in pie and I'm cheap.
You're the new team. Good. Last one left the tank on a quarter and the ashtray full. I don't care about the ashtray.
He's got a tuning fork on his key ring. A dam man with a tuning fork.

passives.line: Tuning fork on the key ring. He's been checking the hum against a note. He's not as sure as he says.
The wagon's oil is clean. He changed it today, before anyone said you were going. He knew.

options.text: Forty-minute cycle. Does the hum hold pitch?

fail.line: It's a pipe. Pipes sing. You want music, the diner's got a jukebox.

options.text: What do we need to know about the wagon?

rate.speaker: hollis
lines: Best rate in Braxton County. Don't tell the county.
Thirty years I've come by this dock. Gus was under the hood the first time. Said hand me the nine-sixteenths. I did. Never left.
That's how it gets you. One wrench.

pitch.speaker: hollis
lines: ...Holds pitch. Shouldn't. Hydraulics drift with the temperature, and it's been the same note since '74.
(He holds up the fork.) A. It's an A. I check it. Don't tell Pearl.
An A. Three notes, and the first one's an A. I'll want the other two.

wagon.speaker: hollis
lines: Second gear sticks cold. Choke's touchy. Heater works if you kick the box under the dash, and only there.
And the radio. Don't fiddle with the dial on the road at night. Gus's rule, not mine. I just never took it off.
A rule about a radio dial. I'll file it under maintenance.

hub.speaker: hollis
lines: Go on. I've a shift at the dam at three and the wagon's done.

static.line: He changed the oil before you said you were going. Ask who told him. Ask if it was the radio.

options.text: Why didn't you ever leave, Hollis?
Same three notes, same pitch, twenty years. You don't think it's the gates.
What happens if you fiddle with the dial?

stayed.speaker: hollis
lines: Nowhere else had a garage and a woman who'd listen to me about pipes.
Then she didn't come back, and somebody had to keep the wagon running for when she did. Dot kept the counter. I kept the wagon.
That's the whole staff list, isn't it.

stayed_fail.speaker: hollis
lines: Work's here. Dam's here. That's a question for people who leave.
Pearl's the one who talks about leaving. Go ask Pearl why she never did either.

gates_truth.speaker: hollis
lines: I think it's the gates 'cause I've got to think something and go down in that spillway every week. Think anything else, you don't come up.
Gus stood on the bank and listened for the rest of it. I listen for the gates. We're both right. Mine lets me sleep.
He's not wrong. He's just chosen which half to hear.

gates_fail.speaker: hollis
lines: You've been in this town a day. I've been in that spillway twenty years. Go drive your case.

dial.speaker: hollis
lines: Nothing you'd put in a report. Gus said the dial finds a station that ain't there, nights, and once it's found it, it don't let go.
I never fiddled. I'm not the fiddling kind. The last team did, and they came back and didn't go out again.
I'll note it as a superstition. Then I'll leave the dial alone.
